question: In a chromatography process, a specific type of plate was prepared using a matrix made from an amorphous and porous form of silicon dioxide known for its tridimensional framework and nanometer‐scale voids, a substance also employed as a matrix in the synthesis of a uranium oxide compound. This compound is produced by subjecting a yellow crystalline substance, which has a slight vinegar odor and serves as a negative stain in electron microscopy, to a heat treatment process with the addition of acetic acid and hydrochloric acid. What is the type of chromatographic plate that was prepared and used to spot dissolved pharmaceutical samples?

Magnesium Oxide is the oxide salt of magnesium with antacid, laxative and vascular smooth muscle relaxant activities. Text:
Ethylene oxide is a flammable gas with a somewhat sweet odor. It dissolves easily in water. Ethylene oxide is a man-made chemical that is used primarily to make ethylene glycol (a chemical used to make antifreeze and polyester). A small amount (less than 1%) is used to control insects in some stored agricultural products and a very small amount is used in hospitals to sterilize medical equipment and supplies.
Ethylene Oxide can cause cancer, developmental toxicity, female reproductive toxicity and male reproductive toxicity according to state or federal government labeling requirements.
Ethylene oxide appears as a clear colorless gas with an ethereal odor with a flash point below 0 °F. Liquid less dense than water. Vapors heavier than air. May polymerize exothermically if heated or contaminated. If the polymerization takes place inside a container, the container may rupture violently. Vapors very toxic. Vapors irritate the eyes, skin, and respiratory system. Prolonged skin contact may result in delayed burns. Used to make other chemicals, as a fumigant and industrial sterilant.

Thin layer chromatography (TLC) is an interesting alternative approach that has been used for drug quantification for many years. It can be performed without the complex fluid flow systems of HPLC and has been shown to achieve comparable results to HPLC down to nM concentrations by scrapping the separated bands of drug off the TLC plate for subsequent quantification by solution-based fluorimetry. Advances in imaging technology have now made it possible to quantify the DOX bands directly on TLC plates through image analysis of the fluorescent bands via consumer smartphones and other devices. Despite its simplicity, and ability to be partially automated for high throughput applications , the TLC process has never been adapted for use in a bedside clinical setting due to the required organic solvents used in developing the plate and the hazardous silica dust material on the plate itself. Currently, the TLC technique is only performed in laboratories with ventilated fume hoods with quantification requiring additional expertise in chemical processing.
